When p>2, balancing residual powers and t↦t^((p−2)/(p−1)) subadditivity force normalized derivative weights <=1/2; Hölder gives repeated-block constant <= (|B|/2)^(1/p). At strictly complementary full-pooling data, a residual-zero coordinate below p=2 gives mean shift h+o(h), while ±1 extreme residuals above p=2 give derivative weights 1/2,1/2; these attain sharp supremal constants locally. Hilbert projection and n<=2 have norm 1. Sources RESULT.md/verify_isotonic.py actually read; numerical tests are not universal proof.
